Honeyed Biscuits for St. Catherine's Day

Served at: St. Catherine's Day

Serves 8-10 (makes about 12 biscuits)Prep 20 minCook 15-18 min

St. Catherine's Day on November 25th is a traditional feast day, particularly celebrated by young, unmarried women known as "Catherinettes." These tender, subtly sweet honeyed biscuits are a comforting treat, perfect for sharing with friends and family, or as a warm offering during community gatherings, embodying the spirit of warmth and camaraderie associated with the day.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (240 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 tablespoon baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, very cold and cut into small cubes
  • 3 tablespoons (45 ml) honey, plus more for drizzling
  • 3/4 cup (180 ml) cold buttermilk

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or lightly grease it.
  2. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and granulated sugar.
  3. Add the cold butter cubes to the dry ingredients. Using a pastry blender, two knives, or your fingertips, cut the butter into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces of butter remaining.
  4. In a separate small bowl, whisk together the 3 tablespoons (45 ml) of honey and the cold buttermilk.
  5. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Stir gently with a fork or spatula until just combined. Do not overmix; the dough will be shaggy.
  6. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Gently pat or roll the dough to about 3/4-inch (2 cm) thickness.
  7. Using a 2-inch (5 cm) round biscuit cutter, cut out biscuits. Press straight down without twisting to ensure a good rise. Gather scraps, gently re-pat, and cut remaining biscuits.
  8. Place the biscuits about 1 inch (2.5 cm) apart on the prepared baking sheet.
  9. Bake for 15-18 minutes, or until golden brown on top and cooked through.
  10. Remove from the oven and immediately brush or drizzle with additional honey while warm.
  11. Serve warm with butter, jam, or more honey.

Tips

  • For extra flaky biscuits, fold the dough over itself 2-3 times before the final patting/rolling.
  • Ensure all dairy ingredients (butter, buttermilk) are very cold for the best texture.
  • If you don't have buttermilk, you can make a substitute by adding 3/4 tablespoon of lemon juice or white vinegar to 3/4 cup (180 ml) of regular milk and letting it sit for 5 minutes.
